note: C's two neighbours on the circle of fifths (keys:1): G and F read off the middle of the circle as 1♯ and 1♭, then the one changed note found on the piano in each key. The keys are the lesson, so there are no moves; each section has one feel to reach or one thing to listen for.

exercise.title: One sharp, one flat
exercise.why: Each place you move round the circle of fifths changes one note of the scale, so the keys next to C are the ones that differ from it by a single sharp or flat.

cells.text:
The circle of fifths below starts on C major, and its middle says "no ♯ ♭". Tap G on the outer ring, one place clockwise from C: the circle moves to G, and the middle now shows 1♯.
Tap C to come back, then tap F, one place the other way, to see 1♭. Then go a few places further each way, and watch the number in the middle.
Each place you move away from C adds one sharp or one flat.
The piano below shows G major. Tap from {{1}} up to the next {{1}}: every key is white but one, {{f-sharp}}, the key's one sharp.

This piano shows F major, with its one flat, {{b-flat}}. Tap up the scale from {{1}}. Then tap {{b-flat}} and the white key just to its right, the B that C major has in its place.
Listen for the one note the flat changed: the rest of the scale is the white keys of C major.
